title: Sport Metrics
description: Sports analytics for coaches and analysts: game data and video, together, the same day.
summary: Sports analytics for coaches and analysts: play-by-play data linked to the exact second of video, ready the same day.
body:
## The problem

Coaches and analysts usually wait one to two days to get the video and data of a game they just played. By the time the numbers arrive, the next game is already on top of them.

## What we're building

Sport Metrics is sports analytics for coaches and analysts of any sport and league. With [Kira](https://github.com/KiraBelak) I'm building a platform that captures every play of a game, links it to the exact second of the video and turns it into reports a coaching staff can actually use.

- **Data you can trust.** We cross-check two independent public sources for each game and rebuild the box score from the play-by-play, so every number can be traced back to a play.
- **Every stat is a clip.** Click a play and the video jumps to that moment.
- **Game reports** for analysts and coaches, with roles and a PDF export to share with the staff.
- Bilingual, English and Spanish.

## My part

I work on the product and the web app: the landing, the game report and its PDF export, and the research behind which data sources we can rely on. Kira leads the video capture engine and the heavy infrastructure.

title: Klai
description: Chrome extension that draws animated, data-driven graphics on top of any live video, from a plain-text command.
summary: Type a command and an AI draws live, animated graphics on top of any video you're watching. Winner of the New Interfaces track at Platanus Hack 26.
body:
## Winner, New Interfaces track: Platanus Hack 26 (CDMX)

Klai (first called Overlai) was built in 48 hours at Platanus Hack 26 in Mexico City, in June 2026, and won the New Interfaces track.

## The idea

What if the graphics you see on a sports broadcast (scores, stats, player cards) could be generated on demand, on top of any video, by just asking for them?

## How it works

- A **Chrome extension** sits on top of the video you're watching.
- You type what you want to see, like "show me this player's season stats".
- A **backend in Next.js** looks up the data on the web and an LLM generates the UI for it, which the extension renders as an animated overlay on the live video.

## What came after

After the hackathon I explored turning it into a product for small sports broadcasts. The honest conclusion was that Klai is a great feature but not a business on its own, and that thinking fed directly into [Sport Metrics](/projects/sport-metrics).

title: justenvs
description: Native macOS app to store and share your projects' environment variables, encrypted.
summary: A native Mac app to keep every project's .env encrypted, unlocked with Touch ID, and shared through zero-knowledge links.
body:
## The problem

Every developer has `.env` files scattered across old projects, pasted in chats and lost when they switch laptops. They hold the most sensitive keys we have, and we treat them like notes.

## What I built

- **A native macOS app** in Swift and SwiftUI. Your environment variables are encrypted on your Mac with CryptoKit, and the key lives in the Keychain behind Touch ID.
- **Zero-knowledge sharing.** Send a teammate a link; the server only ever sees encrypted data it can't read.
- **`.env` sync** with your project folders, so the app stays the source of truth.
- **Auto-updates** with Sparkle and a marketing site at justenvs.app.

## Shipping it

I launched it in June 2026 and shipped releases almost daily to its first users. The launch week included an all-nighter when Apple stopped recognizing the app's bundle ID: I moved to a new one, restored Touch ID and walked users through reinstalling. Shipping a real Mac app taught me signing, notarization and update channels the hard way.

title: Artemisa
description: Free tool that finds where your photos (real or AI deepfakes) are exposed online, without your photo ever leaving your device.
summary: Find out if intimate images of you, real or AI-made, are circulating online, and get the evidence and guidance to act.
body:
## Why

Digital violence in Latin America is not the exception. Deepfakes are overwhelmingly non-consensual sexual content, and most of the victims are women. When it happens, people don't know where their images are, how to prove it or who to call.

## What it does

Built in a weekend at HackLatam (May 2026) with [Kira](https://github.com/KiraBelak) and [Pedro](https://github.com/RoniHY):

- **Your photo never leaves your device.** It's processed locally into a mathematical fingerprint; only that fingerprint is used to search.
- **Scans the open web**: public sites, forums, image boards and reverse image search, looking for real or AI-altered images of you.
- **Evidence you can use**: a downloadable PDF report with URLs, screenshots and metadata to take to a lawyer, an organization or a police report.
- **A legal assistant chat** that explains your rights, the relevant laws and organizations that can help.

## My part

I set up the project's foundation (Next.js, auth, database), built the legal assistant agent with LangGraph and streaming responses, and the PDF evidence report. Kira built the image-scanning engine and Pedro the landing and the defense guide.

title: Koi School
description: A gamified poker academy for beginners: short lessons, quizzes and boss fights, no real money. From fish to dragon.
summary: Learn poker like an RPG: short lessons, quizzes and boss fights, an honest bankroll tracker and an AI coach that reviews your real hands.
body:
## Why

I want to get good at poker, and the serious tools are expensive and confusing. So I built the academy I wanted: something that feels like a game and keeps me honest.

## What's inside

- **Courses as quests**: from fundamentals to postflop, GTO and tournaments, each lesson with its own quiz.
- **Practice and progression** inspired by Codédex: levels, ranks, weekly missions and a koi mascot that evolves into a dragon as you improve.
- **Bankroll tracker** with a tilt check-in on every session and alerts when you're playing above your bankroll.
- **AI coach for real sessions**: upload your hand history and get an analysis of the spots where you lost money.
- **Public range charts**: a free page with all the preflop ranges, rendered server-side for search engines.

## Where it is

It started as Poker Quest, a personal app, and grew into Koi School: a multi-user academy with accounts, profiles and progress tracking. Its motto: from fish to dragon.

title: sweeply
description: Open-source CLI that frees up disk space by safely deleting rebuildable folders from old projects.
summary: An open-source terminal app that finds the node_modules, build folders and caches eating your disk, and tells you which ones are safe to delete.
body:
## The problem

Old projects quietly eat your disk: `node_modules`, `.next`, `dist`, Python virtualenvs, Rust `target`, iOS `Pods`. Tools to delete them exist, but none tell you whether deleting is actually safe.

## What I built

`npx sweeply` opens an interactive terminal UI that scans your machine, groups the dead weight by project and deletes it with confirmation.

- **Multi-ecosystem**: JavaScript, Python, Rust, iOS and more, in one scan.
- **A safety traffic light per project** based on git: green when everything is pushed, yellow when there's local work, red when it's not a repo at all and deleting would be unrecoverable.
- **Bilingual**: English by default, Spanish if your system is in Spanish.

## Shipping it properly

Published on npm with trusted publishing and provenance, a protected `main` branch, CI with type checks and CodeQL, Dependabot and secret scanning. A tool that deletes files has to be boringly trustworthy.

title: πt (Pit)
description: A desktop AI agent you talk to: it listens, plans with Claude, does real work with tools and answers out loud.
summary: A physical AI agent for your desk: push a button, ask for something, and it plans, uses real tools and answers out loud.
body:
## The idea

AI agents live in browser tabs. What if one lived on your desk, and you could just talk to it?

## What we built in 48 hours

With [ampersand](https://github.com/arampersand), at a hackathon in June 2026:

- **The device**: an ESP32-S3 with a ReSpeaker microphone array, a speaker and LED rings that animate while it listens and thinks.
- **The loop**: push to talk → audio streams over WebSocket to a Python backend → Whisper transcribes → Claude makes a plan → it runs real tools → it answers in spoken Spanish.
- **Real tools, not a demo**: it can search and open issues and pull requests on GitHub, hand coding tasks to Claude Code and run a strict allowlist of shell commands like tests and git status.

## What's next

The prototype proved the whole pipeline works end to end, and also hit the limits of the hardware we picked. We're planning a v2 built properly instead of patching the hackathon version.
